title: Alphonso Trent's band, rated A, and why it bypassed New York
summary: He praises Trent's early band and Morgenstern relays why they avoided the Arcadia in New York.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: It's a funny thing, though, Dan, that a band like Alphonso Trent whom I give an A' rating... and I guess I was influenced by the fact that it was the first, you know, organized from band that I heard. Because Trent started/like a five-piece band to go on to become, you know, a twelve-or fourteen-piece band when the conductor was Stuff Smith conducting. I never will forget that first band that I heard in front of Ella B. Moore's theater was something with A. G. Godley playing drums and Snub Mosley playing trombone and Brent Sparks on tuba and T. Holder , trumpet. Holloway, Trent and George Fielding* as the singers.

Well, even a five or six piece band like that...playing together and playing different things and going from one key to the other, and really swinging, you know, this was unusual. And they went on and into strange things. However, as great as they were, and as great as they played together, they didn't come to New York City.

I was talking a little bit to Snub Mosley about that, and Snub said they did come to New York and, but just...I think they were playing theaters or something, and they were asked... Meyer Davis asked them to come into the Arcadia which was competition to the Roseland and he said Trent didn't want to do it because he was afraid of losing his men. He thought

if they were in New York too long the good guys would be, you know... which Snub said they wouldn't do because they all loved Trent and they would have stayed with him, but he was kind of nervous about that, so instead they, you know, went on...
They bypassed New York City for Buffalo. That's amazing. I think if had come to New York history would have been rewritten as far as...
Well everybody who really heard that band talks about how great they were. Just the few records they made, you can hear the...
Well, I don't think the records could ever do them...
No. / You know, because of the inferior quality of recordings in those days. They had to have somebody like that Al Jolson or somebody with them into get any... attention.
